children: Marking its entry into the construction of advanced weapon-intensive platforms, Cochin Shipyard Ltd has laid the keel for the first Next Generation Missile Vessel (NGMV) project being built for the Indian Navy.

Vice Admiral Sanjay Sadhu, Controller of Warship Production and Acquisition from Integrated Headquarters, (Indian Navy) laid the keel on Friday in the presence of Jose V J, Chairman and Managing Director, CSL, Rear Admiral Kapil Mehta, and S Harikrishnan, Director (Operations) CSL. ,
CSL have six Next Generation Missile Vessels (NGMV) in its order book under the contract signed with the Indian Navy on March 30, 2023.

These ships are envisaged as high-speed vessels with formidable array of weapons and sensors including a Surface-to-Surface Missile system, Anti-Missile Defence System, Air Surveillance and Fire Control Radars, said a press release.

The primary role of the NGMV would be to provide offensive capability against enemy warships, merchantmen and land targets. These ships will be capable of conducting maritime strike operations, anti-surface warfare operations and would be a potent instrument of sea denial for enemy ships especially at choke points. In a defensive role, these ships would be employed for local naval defence operations and seaward defence of offshore development area.

The vessels will also be equipped with highly advanced state-of-the-art integrated platform management systems, propulsion machinery, auxiliary machinery, power generation and distribution machinery and damage control machinery etc. The ship will have a complement of total 80 personnel and having a maximum speed of 33 knots.

title: Cochin Shipyard lays keel for Navy’s next generation missile vessels
